comment: Reviewed third-party components that are not Rust crates. gen_third_party_notices.py --check compares the swift entries with platforms/apple/Package.resolved and the nuget entries with platforms/windows/Directory.Packages.props, so a new package fails the policy gate until it is listed here with its licence. Texts live in shared/licenses/texts/.

swift.distribution: statically linked into libFileIDAppleKit.dylib; mlx.metallib built from its kernels
bundled: fmt (MIT, Copyright (c) 2012 - present, Victor Zverovich and {fmt} contributors)

swift.distribution: statically linked into the Mac app helpers; uses the operating system's SQLite (public domain)

copyright: Copyright Apple Inc. and the Swift project authors
Copyright Apple Inc. and the Swift project authors
Copyright Apple Inc. and the Swift project authors
Copyright Apple Inc. and the SwiftCrypto project authors
swift.distribution: statically linked; includes BoringSSL (OpenSSL and ISC licences, notices kept in its source headers) and the Keccak code package

copyright: Copyright Apple Inc. and the Swift project authors
swift.distribution: build-time macro dependency; the Swift Runtime Library Exception applies, nothing ships
vendored at platforms/apple/vendor/onnxruntime-swift-package-manager (LICENSE kept); links the ONNX Runtime 1.24.2 pod archive statically

nuget.distribution: WinUI 3 runtime shipped with the Windows app; Microsoft ships the framework package under its own redistribution terms
nuget.note: Upstream repository microsoft/WindowsAppSDK is MIT; the NuGet package licence text was not re-fetched offline. Confirm on a Windows machine (see shared/docs/LICENSES.md).

nuget.distribution: build-time only; nothing from it is redistributed
Microsoft.Graphics.Win2D.dll shipped with the Windows app
native e_sqlite3 shipped with the Windows app; SQLite itself is public domain
installer build tool; the bootstrapper stub it links into the setup executable is compiled WiX code

native.name: ONNX Runtime
native.distribution: Windows only, opt-in ort-accel builds: onnxruntime.dll built from the pinned source tree (Intel mirror intel/onnxruntime, same tree as microsoft/onnxruntime) without telemetry. Not in macOS or Linux builds and not in the default Windows build (tract CPU)
native.note: ONNX Runtime's own ThirdPartyNotices.txt lists its bundled dependencies (protobuf, Eigen, abseil, re2, onnx, ...) and must travel with the runtime binaries; see shared/docs/LICENSES.md.

native.name: DirectML (Microsoft.AI.DirectML)
native.distribution: DirectML.dll staged unmodified next to the engine (fetch-runtime-deps.ps1, SHA-256 pinned)
native.note: Not MIT. Microsoft's redistributable licence in the NuGet package (LICENSE.txt) permits shipping DirectML.dll with an application; it is a binary under Microsoft's terms and is not relicensed under Apache-2.0.

native.name: ONNX Runtime OpenVINO pack (Intel OpenVINO runtime)
native.distribution: optional Performance Pack and Store bundle; its own licenses/ folder travels with it

native.name: NVIDIA CUDA runtime and cuDNN redistributables
native.distribution: optional CUDA Performance Pack downloaded only after the user accepts the NVIDIA terms (ModelLicenseGate); never part of the default install
native.note: NVIDIA redistributable EULAs, not open source; opt-in with terms shown at install.

native.name: PDFium (bblanchon/pdfium-binaries chromium/7857)
native.distribution: pdfium.dll staged unmodified (SHA-256 pinned); the archive's licenses/ folder lists PDFium's bundled third-party code

native.name: llama.cpp (llama-server)
native.distribution: Linux: built from the pinned source with the outbound-HTTP patch; Windows: SHA-256-pinned Vulkan build. Its THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt (cpp-httplib, nlohmann/json, stb_image, miniaudio, subprocess.h) is staged with it

native.name: whisper.cpp
native.distribution: SHA-256-pinned Windows runtime staged in the Store bundle

native.name: GTK 4, libadwaita, GLib/GIO, Pango, Cairo, GdkPixbuf and their dependencies
native.distribution: linked dynamically (gtk4-rs and libadwaita-rs bindings are MIT; the C libraries are loaded as shared objects). Flatpak, distro and Nix packages use the system or GNOME runtime copies; the AppImage bundles them as replaceable shared libraries
native.note: LGPL: FileID does not modify these libraries. Source is available from the upstream projects and the distribution that supplied them; the AppImage user can replace the bundled .so files because the image can be extracted and run with its own libraries.

native.name: FFmpeg and OpenH264 (optional media runtime)
native.distribution: NOT part of any release artifact: the shared LGPL build (GPL and nonfree disabled, networking compiled out) exists only as a local development bundle with source and licence records; release packaging is blocked until codec patent clearance (stage-media.ps1 refuses CI_RELEASE)
native.note: OpenH264 built from source does not carry Cisco's binary patent grant.

native.name: Archivo (variable font)
native.distribution: Archivo-Variable.ttf bundled with the app and website; Archivo-OFL.txt sits beside it

native.name: Instrument Serif
copyright: Copyright 2022 The Instrument Serif Project Authors (https://github.com/Instrument/instrument-serif)
native.distribution: InstrumentSerif-Regular/Italic.ttf bundled with the app and website; InstrumentSerif-OFL.txt sits beside them
